We start with the ratio $4:6$ and write it as a fraction:

$$
\frac{4}{6}
$$

So the numerator represents the left-hand entry ($4$), and the denominator represents the right-hand entry ($6$).

We can generate equivalent ratios by finding equivalent fractions:

- To create a numerator of $2,$ we divide the numerator and denominator of our fraction by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4÷2}{6÷2}=\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

- To create a denominator of $18,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator of the previous fraction by $6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\times 6}{3\times 6} & =\frac{12}{18}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we fill in the ratio table:

| $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- |
| $4$ | $6$ |
| $12$ | $18$ |
